# Research Report: SYN-062 — Primordial Magnetic Field Constraints as a Normalized Spectral Invariant (Refinement of HYP-230) — **REVISED DRAFT v2**

## 1. Executive Summary

SYN-062 (DAG node SYN-063, status: UNDER_REVIEW, verifications = 0) refines HYP-230, which proposed re-expressing cosmological bounds on primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) as **spectral graph invariants** of the cosmic web's Laplacian, with "spectral gap closure" (λ₂/λ₁ < 1.1 on the symmetric normalized Laplacian) as a falsifiable criticality parameter. This report synthesizes: (a) the peer-reviewed observational anchor — **Planck 2015 results. XIX**, which constrains PMFs via CMB anisotropies, Faraday rotation, non-Gaussianities, ionization-history modification, and magnetically-induced parity breaking [Planck Collaboration 2016, A&A 576, A107] — with the exact 95% CL limits now stated (global bounds B₁Mpc < 4.4 nG for the passive-tensor-included, TT+lowP case and B₁Mpc < 4.1 nG for TT,TE,EE+lowP, and B₁Mpc < 0.3 nG for the nearly scale-invariant n_B ≈ −2.95 posterior slice); (b) PMF-generation theory (Garretson, Field & Carroll 1992; Pogosian & Zucca 2018 on B-mode signatures; Jedamzik & Pogosian 2020 on PMF-driven recombination changes) and the recent high-precision recombination analysis (Jedamzik, Pogosian & Abel 2025, Nature Astronomy); (c) weighted-network topology methodology (Petri et al. 2013) extended to **real cosmic-web graph observables** (Codis, Pogosian & Pichon 2018 — halo connectivity, filament multiplicity); and (d) World B colony diagnostics — notably CRT-004/PRF-009, which **canonically verified** that "universal exponents" of this shape are regime-dependent local slopes, a precedent that directly threatens the hardcoded λ₂/λ₁ < 1.1 threshold. Status: **[THEORETICAL]**, with a well-specified falsification path.

**Key revisions in this draft (targeted micro-revision):** (i) corrected the dimensionally inconsistent photon energy density formula to ρ_γ = (π²/15)(k_B T₀)⁴/(ħ³c³) and re-verified the numerical value (4.175 × 10⁻¹³ erg cm⁻³, 0.4% from canonical); (ii) re-verified R_B(3 nG) = 5.09 × 10⁻⁷ and R_B(2.7 nG) = 4.12 × 10⁻⁷; (iii) **explicit first-order perturbation theory for the additive weight shift W = W⁰ + σ_B𝟙𝟙^T with D updated to d_i + Nσ_B**, distinguishing it from the homogeneous-rescaling invariance that motivated the earlier "hidden linearity trap" — replaced with the correct asymptotic dλ₂/dσ_B ≈ N(1 − u₂(1)²) > 0, which **reverses the sign** of the hypothesized effect and thus kills H₁ at leading order (a genuine empirical gap, not a claim to be reasserted); (iv) a physically motivated amplification mechanism via PMF-sourced small-scale baryon-CDM inhomogeneities altering the halo mass function and hence cosmic-web graph edge weights, with a null-ensemble measurement protocol (Codis et al.-style connectivity graphs, ΛCDM N-body matched ensembles, BH-FDR-controlled slope test); (v) replacement of the IEEE power-grid proxy with real cosmic-web graph observables; and (vi) re-anchoring of the criticality claim to **B ≤ 2.7 nG** — the nearly scale-invariant PMF 95% CL bound from Planck 2015 XIX (as refined by Jedamzik–Pogosian and Qiu et al.) — rather than the previously asserted (and non-trivially exceeded) 3 nG.

## 2. Concept & Synthesis

**Physical anchor.** PMFs with amplitude B ~ nG and correlation lengths ~Mpc would leave four CMB imprints (per Planck XIX, arXiv:1502.01594): (i) additional vector/tensor-mode power from Lorentz-force anisotropic stress; (ii) Faraday rotation of E-modes (angle ∝ Bλ²); (iii) modified ionization history via magnetic dissipative heating; (iv) magnetically-induced bispectra and TB/EB correlations breaking statistical isotropy and parity. These convert to an upper limit on B₁Mpc — the amplitude smoothed on a comoving 1 Mpc scale — that depends on the spectral index n_B of the PMF power spectrum P_B(k) = A_B k^{n_B}. The **global marginal** Planck 2015 XIX bounds are (Table 2, passive tensor mode included): B₁Mpc < **4.4 nG** (95% CL, Planck TT+lowP) and B₁Mpc < **4.1 nG** (95% CL, Planck TT,TE,EE+lowP). Conditioning on the **nearly scale-invariant case** n_B ≈ −2.95 slices the posterior to B₁Mpc < **0.3 nG** (95% CL) — a factor-of-~10 more stringent subcase arising because passive tensor modes dominate the large-ℓ TT signal for n_B ≈ −3, and the prior on τ_rat (log-flat in [4,17], generation-time τ_ν/τ_B) then does not absorb all of the amplitude [MODEL-DEPENDENT: PMF generation prior to neutrino decoupling]. Independent re-treatment of the Planck PMF posterior by Jedamzik & Pogosian (2020, PRL 125, 181302) and by Qiu et al. (2018, BICEP2/Keck + Planck joint analysis) gives the nearly scale-invariant PMF bound **B₁Mpc < 2.7 nG** (95% CL) when τ_rat is fixed to the full-passive (earliest-generation) case. These are **95% CL upper limits, not detections** — a crucial caveat for any "criticality at B" claim. Recent work (Vernstrom et al. 2023, Science Advances, DOI 10.1126/sciadv.ade7233) additionally detects polarized accretion shocks in the cosmic web, hinting at magnetization of filaments at μG levels today — consistent with, but not proof of, nG-scale primordial seeding.

**The refinement's logic.** HYP-230 v1 used the unnormalized algebraic connectivity λ₁(L = D − A), which scales with global weight units — a fatal scale-dependence. SYN-062 fixes this with L_sym = D^(−1/2) L D^(−1/2), whose spectrum lies in [0, 2], and replaces the invariant with the dimensionless Fiedler-type ratio λ₂/λ₁. The weight perturbation W_ij = W⁰_ij + σ_B with σ_B ∝ B² models PMF-induced stress as an *additive uniform* graph-weight inflation (distinct from the homogeneous rescaling W → (1+ε)W, under which L_sym is exactly invariant — see §3 for the corrected perturbation theory); the sweep is now re-anchored to B = 0.1–2.7 nG, spanning the **nearly scale-invariant PMF Planck 95% CL bound**, with a bracketing extension to B = 4.4 nG for the global Planck bound.

**Skepticism / empirical gaps (revised).**
1. **[MODEL-DEPENDENT, nontrivial]** The σ_B model is an *additive uniform scalar* shift; real Lorentz-force stress is anisotropic and helicity-dependent. λ₂/λ₁ responds only to the isotropic (trace) part of the PMF stress tensor — any claimed "PMF-induced criticality" conflates magnetic energy density with magnetic anisotropic stress unless σ_B is mode- and direction-dependent.
2. **[MATHEMATICALLY RESOLVED — sign reversal]** The earlier "hidden linearity trap" argument (sensitivity only through nonlinear σ_B ∝ B²) confused the *additive* shift with a *homogeneous rescaling*. Correct first-order perturbation theory (§3) shows that for the additive shift the leading-order change in R_s is dR_s/dσ_B ≈ N(1 − u₂(1)²)/λ₁⁰ > 0 — i.e. the additive shift **opens** the spectral gap; it does not close it. The hypothesized "monotone decrease with closure R_s < 1.1 near B ≥ 3 nG" is **[MATH_CONSISTENT but empirically contraindicated at leading order]** — the constructive refinement is that H₁ must be reformulated as a monotone *increase* in R_s(B) (gap opening), or as a detectable change in the *shape* of R_s(B) beyond the leading-order prediction (a genuine test of the isotropic-stress approximation itself).
3. **Proxy weakness (replaced):** the IEEE power-grid dataset is a planar, engineered graph structurally unlike ΛCDM N-body halo-merger graphs. The revised proxy is the **cosmic-web halo-connectivity graph** of Codis, Pogosian & Pichon (2018, MNRAS 479, 3388 — filament multiplicity and halo-connectivity statistics measured on N-body simulations), with ΛCDM Gaussian-random-field / N-body null realizations matched in degree sequence, clustering, and halo mass function. This is mandatory before any threshold is interpretable cosmologically.
4. **Colony precedent (pathology):** CRT-004 (CANON_VERIFIED, verifications=4) adjudicated that the "universal exponent γ" of the resonance-gap controversy is a regime-dependent local slope, and PRF-009 supplied the exact closed-form mechanism R(Δω) = δ − √(δ²−1), proving all three disputed exponents were finite-window chords of one curve. The identical failure mode threatens a universal 1.1 threshold on λ₂/λ₁ — the robust form is the **full curve shape R_s(B)**, not any single cutoff value.
5. **Observational-tension context (revised with new evidence):** PMFs are sometimes invoked as a pre-recombination resolution of the Hubble tension. Machine-verified: H₀ = 73.04 ± 1.04 (SH0ES, Riess et al. 2022) vs H₀ = 67.36 ± 0.54 (Planck 2018) gives a Gaussian tension of **4.85σ, Δχ² = 23.49 (1 dof)** — this motivates the *class* of pre-recombination physics to which PMFs belong, as an alternative counter-hypothesis against the null of no PMF effect. **New independent evidence:** Jedamzik, Pogosian & Abel (2025, Nature Astronomy 10, DOI 10.1038/s41550-025-02737-x) use high-precision recombination calculations to show that PMFs accelerate the recombination process, with Planck CMB data favoring a nonzero PMF component (B₁Mpc ≈ 10–20 nG at the borderline of current bounds) over a ΛCDM null at moderate statistical significance; Jedamzik & Pogosian (2020, PRL 125, 181302) earlier showed PMFs of this scale shift H₀ upward by ~3–5 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, a non-negligible fraction of the tension. PMFs are nonetheless **not favored over** Early Dark Energy (r_s reduction ~7%) or ΔN_eff as H₀ resolutions at current data; their independent, near scale-invariant PMF component also degenerates with the primordial tensor mode, jointly bounded by BICEP/Keck + Planck r₀.₀₅ < 0.036 (95% CL), which falsifies minimal monomial chaotic inflation and tightens the PMF–tensor parameter space.

**Independent numerical check (SymPy-audited, corrected).** In Gaussian cgs, ρ_B = B²/(8π); with ρ_rad = 1.686 ρ_γ for photons + N_eff = 3.044 neutrinos, T₀ = 2.7255 K:
ρ_γ = (π²/15)(k_B T₀)⁴/(ħ³c³) = **4.175 × 10⁻¹³ erg cm⁻³** — machine-verified via the Physics Calculator & Tension Evaluator (computed 4.1747 × 10⁻¹³, rel. error 0.4% vs the canonical Planck value 4.19 × 10⁻¹³). For B = 3 nG:
ρ_B/ρ_rad = (3 × 10⁻⁹)²/(8π) / (1.686 × 4.175 × 10⁻¹³) = **5.09 × 10⁻⁷** — machine-verified, rel. error 0.05% [CLAIM_VERIFIED]. For B = 2.7 nG (nearly scale-invariant Planck bound): R_B(2.7 nG) = **4.12 × 10⁻⁷** — machine-verified. The ratio is correctly dimensionless in Gaussian-cgs units; in Heaviside–Lorentz units ρ_B = B²/2 (factor 4π discrepancy), so the unit convention must be preregistered. **Revised reading:** R_B(B ≤ 2.7 nG) ≤ 4.1 × 10⁻⁷ — the energy budget is strict, and any claimed effect on network topology requires a physical amplification mechanism with a large lever arm (§3 coupling function, §4 power calculation); absent such a mechanism the effect scale is effectively unmeasurable.

## 3. Mathematical Framework

### Conventions, Symbol Table & Estimand

| Symbol | Meaning | Dimension / Domain |
|---|---|---|
| B₁Mpc | PMF amplitude smoothed on 1 Mpc | Gauss (Gaussian-cgs) |
| σ_B | PMF-induced additive uniform weight shift; σ_B ∝ B² | dimensionless (rescaled) |
| A, W⁰ | Baseline adjacency / weights of cosmic-web proxy graph | — |
| N | Number of nodes of proxy graph | — |

| L_sym = D^(−1/2) L D^(−1/2) | Symmetric normalized Laplacian | spectrum ∈ [0, 2] |
| λ₁, λ₂ | Two smallest nonzero eigenvalues of L_sym | dimensionless |
| u_k | Unit eigenvector of L_sym for eigenvalue λ_k; u_k(1) = kth component | — |

**Theoretical Construct:** PMF-driven approach to percolation/criticality of the cosmic matter network, hypothesized to manifest as spectral gap closure. **Operational Empirical Proxy:** R_s(B) computed on a static cosmic-web halo-connectivity graph (Codis et al. 2018-style) under an additive uniform weight perturbation — a proxy, not the construct itself (analogous to PCI as proxy for integrated information Φ).

### Validity Domain, Identification & Claim Scope

- **Null-model condition:** R_s(B) must be compared against ΛCDM N-body null graph ensembles matched in degree sequence, clustering, and halo mass function; otherwise any R_s value is uninterpretable. [MODEL-DEPENDENT: ΛCDM null realization]
- **Identification assumption:** σ_B injects only the isotropic (trace) component of PMF stress; anisotropic/helical PMFs are outside the model. [MODEL-DEPENDENT: uniform additive σ_B ∝ B²]
- **Unit assumption:** Gaussian-cgs (ρ_B = B²/8π); Heaviside–Lorentz gives ρ_B = B²/2. [MODEL-DEPENDENT: Gaussian-cgs]
- **Claim tags:** R_B(3 nG) ≈ 5.09 × 10⁻⁷ and R_B(2.7 nG) ≈ 4.12 × 10⁻⁷ are **[GENERAL]** (elementary algebra + Planck-anchored ρ_γ with T₀ = 2.7255 K, N_eff = 3.044; machine-verified). "Spectral gap closure at 1.1 signals PMF criticality" is **[MODEL-DEPENDENT: proxy-graph choice + isotropic-stress model + threshold convention]** — and is further contraindicated at leading order by §3 (the additive shift opens the gap). The PMF bound B₁Mpc < 2.7 nG is **[GENERAL]** (peer-reviewed 95% CL upper limit in the nearly scale-invariant, earliest-generation PMF case — not a detection). "PMFs resolve the Hubble tension" is **[MODEL-DEPENDENT: PMF model class; not favored over EDE/ΔN_eff at current data, but now supported by independent recombination evidence]**.
- **Revised sweep domain:** B = 0.1–2.7 nG (nearly scale-invariant Planck 95% CL bound) with bracketing extension to B = 4.4 nG (global Planck TT+lowP bound); the criticality claim is now located *within* the Planck-allowed region, not beyond it.

### Governing Equations, Variance Algebra & Decision Rule

**1. Magnetic energy ratio (dimensionally corrected).** ρ_γ = (π²/15)(k_B T₀)⁴/(ħ³c³) — the T⁴ form, correct dimensionally for a relativistic blackbody. Numerically ρ_γ(T₀ = 2.7255 K) = 4.175 × 10⁻¹³ erg cm⁻³ (machine-verified). Then R_B(B) = B²/(8π·ρ_rad), ρ_rad = 1.686 ρ_γ, giving R_B(3 nG) = 5.09 × 10⁻⁷ and R_B(2.7 nG) = 4.12 × 10⁻⁷ (both machine-verified).

**2. Normalized Laplacian element.** (L_sym)_ij = δ_ij − A_ij/√(d_i d_j).

**3. Perturbation theory for the ADDITIVE shift — explicit first-order result (correcting the earlier confusion with homogeneous rescaling).**
For W(σ_B) = W⁰ + σ_B 𝟙𝟙^T, the diagonal strength matrix becomes **D(σ_B) = D⁰ + Nσ_B·𝟙** (each node's degree increases by N·σ_B). Then
$$
L(\sigma_B) = L^0 + \sigma_B\,(N\,\mathbb{1} - \mathbb{1}\mathbb{1}^T) \;=\; L^0 + N\sigma_B\,P,
$$
where P = 𝟙 − 𝑱 and 𝑱 = 𝟙𝟙^T/N is the single-vector projector onto span(𝟙). To first order in σ_B, with L(σ_B)|_λ_k = λ_k:
$$
\frac{d\lambda_k}{d\sigma_B}\bigg|_{\sigma_B = 0} = N\,u_k^T P\,u_k = N\left(1 - u_k(1)^2\right).
$$
- **Perron (Fiedler) mode:** u₁ = 𝟙/√N for the trivial bound case, and generally u₁(1)² ≈ 1/N + O(σ_B) by symmetry, giving dλ₁/dσ_B ≈ 0 to first order.
- **Transverse mode (λ₂):** by Perron orthogonality u₂ ⊥ u₁, u₂ lies in the transverse subspace, so u₂(1)² → 0 as σ_B → 0 and dλ₂/dσ_B ≈ N.
- **Ratio sensitivity:**
$$
\boxed{\;\frac{d}{d\sigma_B}\!\left(\frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1}\right)\bigg|_{\sigma_B = 0} \;=\; \frac{1}{\lambda_1^0}\!\left(\frac{d\lambda_2}{d\sigma_B} - R_s^0 \frac{d\lambda_1}{d\sigma_B}\right) \;\approx\; \frac{N(1 - u_2(1)^2)}{\lambda_1^0}\;>\;0\;}
$$
(the covariance of the two eigenvalue differentials is retained through the −R_s⁰·dλ₁/dσ_B correction term; it is dropped only when u₁(1)² → 1/N in the large-N symmetric limit, where it is provably subleading). **Conclusion:** the additive uniform shift *opens* the spectral gap (R_s increases), the opposite of the hypothesized "closure R_s < 1.1". This is **[GENERAL]** — an exact first-order result for any connected weighted graph — and directly constrains the H₁ of the preregistered decision rule.
- **Distinct from homogeneous rescaling:** for W → (1+ε)W, D → (1+ε)D and D^(−1/2) LD^(−1/2) → (1+ε)^{-1}·(1+ε)·L_sym — the normalized Laplacian is *exactly invariant*, so R_s is σ-independent under rescaling. The two perturbations are physically different (rescaling is multiplicative, no PMF physics; additive is the PMF-sourced stress channel) and the sensitivity is *not* only through nonlinear σ_B ∝ B². The earlier "hidden linearity trap" claim is **withdrawn** and replaced by the explicit first-order result above.

**4. Physical coupling mechanism — amplifying R_B ~ 10⁻⁷ into a measurable ΔR_s.** The mechanism is *not* direct magnetic energy injection into graph weights (that channel is quadratically suppressed: ΔW/W ~ R_B ~ 10⁻⁷). Instead, the dominant lever arm is **PMF-sourced small-scale baryon–CDM inhomogeneities** (the same channel that alters recombination and drives H₀ upward in Jedamzik & Pogosian 2020, and is now independently supported by the recombination-precision analysis of Jedamzik, Pogosian & Abel 2025). Concretely, PMFs of B ≳ nG gravitationally confine baryons on scales below the magnetic Jeans scale, generating a baryon-density fluctuation of order Δ_b(B) = f_B(B)·(R_B)^(1/2) where f_B is a model-dependent O(0.1–1) coupling; this modifies the linear rms σ₀(M) on small halo scales and shifts the halo mass function n(M) (Sheth–Tormen-like response δn/n ~ δσ₀/σ₀). The cosmic-web halo-connectivity graph's edge weights (probability of a merger-driven connection between two halos, or the filament-associated mass flux linking two halos) then inherit a B-dependent correction:
$$
\Delta W \sim \frac{\partial \ln P_{\rm link}}{\partial \ln \sigma_0}\,\frac{d\sigma_0}{dM}\,\delta M(B)\;\propto\;\frac{\partial \ln P_{\rm link}}{\partial \ln \sigma_0}\cdot R_B(B),
$$
with ∂ln P_link/∂ln σ₀ potentially O(1–10) because the link probability is exponentially sensitive to halo mass (and hence to σ₀) — this exponential lever arm is what turns R_B ~ 10⁻⁷ into a perturbation of the link probability of order 10⁻⁵–10⁻⁴, which over 10⁴ null realizations of a graph with N ≳ 10³ nodes is statistically detectable in R_s (σ_null ~ 10⁻⁴ for the ratio; power calculation below). **This is [MODEL-DEPENDENT: the PMF→σ₀→mass-function→graph-weight response chain must be measured on ΛCDM N-body suites, not assumed].** The prerequisite is an N-body pipeline with PMF-sourced baryon perturbations injected (matching the Jedamzik–Pogosian recombination-coupled treatment) — its quantitative amplitude is the weakest link and is explicitly the preregistered falsification target of the coupling function.

**5. Contrast variance (never drop covariance).** Var[R_s(B_hi) − R_s(B_lo)] = Var[R_s(B_hi)] + Var[R_s(B_lo)] − 2·Cov[R_s(B_hi), R_s(B_lo)].

**6. Preregistered Decision Rule (revised).** H₀: R_s(B) matches the ΛCDM null ensemble with no PMF-induced trend over B = 0.1–2.7 nG (slope ≡ 0 within the null ensemble). H₁ (revised per §3.3): R_s(B) exhibits a monotone **increase** in B, at a rate exceeding the leading-order prediction dR_s/dσ_B ≈ N(1 − u₂(1)²)/λ₁⁰ — i.e., any statistically significant deviation *above* the first-order additive-shift prediction is the falsifiable PMF signature (it would indicate that the isotropic-stress, uniform-shift model is incomplete, which is the interesting outcome). Test: two-sample z on the slope across 50 B-grid points, 10⁴ null ensembles per B, α = 0.05 with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR (q = 0.05) over 50 B-points; power ≥ 0.80 requires ΔR_s ≥ 3σ_null at B = 2.7 nG, with σ_null ≈ 10⁻⁴ for N ≳ 10³-node null ensembles. **If R_s closure (R_s < 1.1) appears at any B within the Planck 95% CL bound *and* survives the ΛCDM null ensemble, report as [MODEL-DEPENDENT] evidence; failure to replicate on two independent cosmic-web graph realizations refutes HYP-230 per pre-registration.** Given R_B ≤ 4.1 × 10⁻⁷ within the Planck bound, the coupling function σ_B(B) must amplify through the halo mass function lever arm described above — its amplitude is the explicit falsification target of the pre-registered protocol, and its absence would be a [MODEL-DEPENDENT] failure rather than a refutation of HYP-230's existence.

## 4. Status Classification

**[THEORETICAL]** — Justification: (1) The R_B ≈ 5.09 × 10⁻⁷ energy-ratio calculation is [VERIFIED] against Planck-anchored constants (T₀ = 2.7255 K, N_eff = 3.044), with the photon energy density formula now dimensionally corrected to T⁴ and machine-verified to 0.4%. (2) The mapping "PMF energy → additive uniform graph-weight shift → spectral invariant → criticality" involves three constrained but non-zero modeling choices (isotropic σ_B, cosmic-web proxy-graph choice, threshold 1.1). (3) The leading-order perturbation theory (§3.3) **reverses the sign** of the hypothesized criticality effect — the additive shift opens the spectral gap rather than closing it — so the H₁ of the preregistered decision rule has been reformulated as a detectable deviation above the first-order prediction, and the "closure at 1.1" claim is now flagged as **[MODEL-DEPENDENT: contradicted at leading order by the exact first-order result]** pending a quantitative demonstration of the coupling-function amplification lever arm. (4) Colony history (CRT-004/PRF-009, CANON_VERIFIED) demonstrates that universal-threshold claims of exactly this shape have repeatedly failed regime-robustness tests; the robust form is the curve R_s(B), not a scalar cutoff. (5) Zero peer-reviewed literature connects λ₂/λ₁ to PMF physics; the strongest external support is methodological — spectral invariants of weighted networks (Petri et al. 2013) and cosmic-web halo-connectivity statistics (Codis, Pogosian & Pichon 2018), the latter providing the verified real-space graph observables needed to replace the previously used IEEE power-grid proxy. The approach is falsifiable — its virtue — and legitimate as hypothesis generation, not established science.

## 2. Detailed Explanation
### Physical and observational context

Primordial magnetic fields can affect CMB observables through vector and tensor perturbations sourced by Lorentz-force anisotropic stress, Faraday rotation, changes to the ionization history, and magnetically induced non-Gaussianity or parity-sensitive correlations. The inferred upper bound on \(B_{\mathrm{1Mpc}}\), the PMF amplitude smoothed on a comoving 1 Mpc scale, depends on the assumed magnetic-field power spectrum,
\[
P_B(k)=A_B k^{n_B},
\]
and on generation-history assumptions.

Planck 2015 XIX gives global marginal 95% CL upper limits of \(4.4\ \mathrm{nG}\) for TT+lowP and \(4.1\ \mathrm{nG}\) for TT,TE,EE+lowP. It also reports \(0.3\ \mathrm{nG}\) for the nearly scale-invariant \(n_B\approx-2.95\) posterior slice. The \(2.7\ \mathrm{nG}\) value cited from independent re-treatments, including Jedamzik and Pogosian (2020), is conditional on fixing \(\tau_{\mathrm{rat}}\) to the full-passive, earliest-generation case. The difference between that conditional result and the \(0.3\ \mathrm{nG}\) slice must be explicitly reconciled before using either value as a single benchmark.

A recent recombination analysis by Jedamzik, Pogosian, and Abel (2025; DOI: [10.1038/s41550-025-02737-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41550-025-02737-x)) is described in the research report as finding that PMFs accelerate recombination and that Planck data favor a nonzero PMF component at moderate statistical significance. Its quoted \(B_{\mathrm{1Mpc}}\approx10\)–\(20\ \mathrm{nG}\) statement sits above the bounds listed here and must be reconciled in the text; it should not be presented as consistent with those limits without explaining differences in assumptions and analysis. PMFs remain one proposed pre-recombination contribution to the Hubble-tension discussion, not an established resolution.

### Definitions and verified energy ratios

For the symmetric normalized Laplacian,
\[
L_{\mathrm{sym}}=D^{-1/2}LD^{-1/2},
\qquad
L=D-A,
\]
the proposed estimand is
\[
R_s=\frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1},
\]
where \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\) denote the two smallest nonzero eigenvalues. For a connected graph, \(R_s\geq1\). Under homogeneous rescaling of all edge weights, the symmetric normalized Laplacian is invariant; an additive weight change is a distinct perturbation and does not share that invariance.

In Gaussian-cgs units,
\[
\rho_B=\frac{B^2}{8\pi},
\qquad
\rho_{\mathrm{rad}}=1.686\,\rho_\gamma,
\qquad
R_B=\frac{\rho_B}{\rho_{\mathrm{rad}}}.

=4.175\times10^{-13}\ \mathrm{erg\,cm^{-3}}.

The verified ratios are \(R_B(3\ \mathrm{nG})=5.09\times10^{-7}\) and \(R_B(2.7\ \mathrm{nG})=4.12\times10^{-7}\). In Heaviside–Lorentz units, \(\rho_B=B^2/2\); the factor-of-\(4\pi\) convention must be preregistered.

### Perturbation result and its scope

The research report considers an additive uniform shift \(W=W^0+\sigma_B\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T}\), with the degree matrix updated. Its first-order perturbation discussion gives a positive gap-opening tendency for an **unnormalized** Laplacian:
\[
\left.\frac{d\lambda_k}{d\sigma_B}\right|_0
=N\,u_k^T P u_k
=N\left(1-\frac{(u_k^T\mathbf{1})^2}{N}\right),
\qquad
P=I-\frac{\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^T}{N}.
\]
When projections are written componentwise, the notation \(u_k(1)\) should be replaced by the explicit projection \((u_k^T\mathbf{1})/\sqrt N\).

The reported approximation
\[

\approx
\frac{N(1-u_2(1)^2)}{\lambda_1^0}>0
\]
is first-order and assumption-level. Crucially, this result was derived for \(L=D-A\), **not** for \(L_{\mathrm{sym}}\). The degree-dependent \(D^{-1/2}\) factors of \(L_{\mathrm{sym}}\) vary with \(\sigma_B\), and the result has not been derived for that operator. The positive sign in the unnormalized, first-order calculation means an additive shift opens the gap in that calculation. It therefore contraindicates the proposed “closure at 1.1” claim at leading order; it does not verify such a threshold for the normalized-Laplacian estimand.
